During the pendency of any hearing or appeal of a determination that a dog is a dangerous or vicious dog as provided for in this section, the owner of such dog shall cause such dog to be confined at the expense of such owner of such dog, at a veterinary hospital, licensed kennel facility, the animal services division, the animal shelter, or in a proper enclosure deemed suitable by the animal services officer.
(k) Authority of animal services officer to confiscate and confine. If an owner fails or refuses to abide by subsection (j) of this section, the animal services officer is authorized and empowered to impound such animal, confine it at the expense of such owner at a veterinary hospital, kennel facility, the animal services division, the animal shelter, or a proper enclosure deemed suitable by the animal services officer during the pendency of any hearing or appeal mentioned in this section.
(l) Retrieval of dog from veterinary hospital. After notification from the animal control board that a dog has been determined to be a dangerous dog or vicious dog, the owner of such dog shall have three business days within which to pick up the dog from the veterinary hospital or other confinement facility, provided the owner is in compliance with all requirements of the animal control ordinance.
(m) Any dog classified prior to July 1, 2012, as a potentially dangerous dog in this state shall on and after that date be classified as a dangerous dog under this division. Any dog classified prior to July 1, 2012, as a dangerous dog or vicious dog in this state shall on and after that date be classified as a vicious dog under this division.
(Ord. of 4-15-2025)
259:
(a) It is unlawful for an owner to have or possess within the city a classified dog without a certificate of registration issued in accordance with the provisions of this section. Certificates of registration shall be nontransferable and shall be issued to a person 18 years of age or older. Each classified dog must be separately registered with the city and issued a separate certificate of registration. No more than one certificate of registration shall be issued per domicile, regardless of whether such certificate of registration is for a dangerous dog or a vicious dog.
(b) Subject to the additional requirements of this article, a certificate of registration shall be issued once the animal services officer determines that the following requirements have been met:
(1) The owner has maintained a proper enclosure designed to securely confine the dangerous dog on the owner's property (which shall not include any electronic animal confinement system); and
(2) Clearly visible warning signs have been posted at all entrances to the premises where the dog resides, including a sign issued by the animal services division indicating the dog's classification number.
(c) Except as otherwise provided in this article, a certificate of registration for a vicious dog shall be issued if the animal services officer determines that the following requirements have been met:
(1) The owner has maintained a proper enclosure designed to securely confine the vicious dog on the owner's property (which shall not include any electronic animal confinement system);
(2) Clearly visible warning signs have been posted at all entrances to the premises where the dog resides;
(3) A microchip containing an identification number and capable of being scanned has been injected under the skin between the shoulder blades of the dog; and
(4) The owner maintains and can provide proof of general or specific liability insurance in the amount of at least $50,000.00 or the maximum amount authorized by state law issued by an insurer authorized to transact business in this state insuring the owner of the vicious dog against liability for any bodily injury or property damage caused by the vicious dog.
(d) The owner of a classified dog shall notify the animal services division, within 24 hours if the dog is on the loose, is unconfined, has attacked a human, has died or been euthanized, or has been sold or relocated. If the dog has been sold or relocated, the owner shall also provide the animal services officer with the name, address, and telephone number of the new owner of the dog and of the effective date of the transfer. Any transferee of a dangerous dog shall be presumed to have notice of the dog's classification as such. A vicious dog shall not be transferred, sold, or donated to any other person unless it is relinquished to a governmental facility or veterinarian to be euthanized.
(e) The owner of a classified dog shall notify the animal services division if the owner is moving out of the city. The owner of a classified dog who moves to the city from another jurisdiction within the State of Georgia shall register the classified dog with the city within ten days of becoming a resident and notify the animal services division of the jurisdiction from which he or she moved. The owner of a similarly classified dog who is a new resident of the state shall register the dog as required in this section within 30 days after becoming a resident.
(f) Issuance of a certificate of registration or renewal of a certificate of registration by the animal services division in the city does not warrant or guarantee that the requirements specified in this section are maintained by the owner of a classified dog on a continuous basis following the date of the issuance of the initial certificate of registration or following the date of any annual renewal of such certificate.
(g) An animal services officer is authorized to make whatever inquiry is deemed necessary to ensure compliance with the provisions of this article. Pursuant to state law, law enforcement agencies, including those of the city will cooperate with animal services officers in enforcing the provisions of this article.
(h) An annual fee, which may be set from time to time in addition to any regular dog licensing fees shall be paid to register classified dogs as required by this article. Certificates of registration shall be renewed on an annual basis. At the time of the annual renewal of a certificate of registration, an animal services officer shall require evidence from the owner or make such investigation as may be necessary to verify that the classified dog is continuing to be confined in a proper enclosure and that the owner is continuing to comply with other provisions of the animal control ordinance. Failure to renew a certificate of registration within ten days of the renewal date or initial classification date shall constitute a violation of this article.
(i) No certificate of registration shall be issued to any person who has been convicted of two or more violations of this article.
(j) No certificate of registration for a vicious dog shall be issued to any person (or to any person residing with such person) who has been convicted (from the time of conviction until two years after completion of his or her sentence) of:
(1) A serious violent felony as defined in O.C.G.A. § 17-10-6.1;
(2) The felony of dogfighting as provided for in O.C.G.A. § 16-12-37 or the felony of aggravated cruelty to animals as provided for in O.C.G.A. § 16-12-4; or
(3) A felony involving trafficking in cocaine, illegal drugs, marijuana, methamphetamine, or ecstasy as provided for in O.C.G.A. § 16-13-31.1.
(Ord. of 4-15-2025)
260:
(a) It shall be unlawful for an owner of a dangerous dog to permit the dog to be off the owner's property unless:
(1) The dog is restrained by a leash not to exceed six feet in length and is under the immediate physical control of a person capable of preventing the dog from engaging any other human or animal when necessary;
(2) The dog is contained in a closed and locked cage or crate; or
(3) The dog is working or training as a hunting dog, herding dog, or predator control dog.
(b) It shall be unlawful for an owner of a vicious dog to permit the dog to be:
(1) Outside an enclosure designed to securely confine the vicious dog while on the owner's property or outside a securely locked and enclosed pen, fence, or other structure suitable to prevent the vicious dog from leaving such property unless:
a. The dog is muzzled and restrained by a leash not to exceed six feet in length and is under the immediate physical control of a person capable of preventing the dog from engaging any other human or animal when necessary; or
b. The dog is contained in a closed and locked cage or crate; or
(2) Unattended with minors.
(c) No person shall be the owner of more than one vicious dog.
(Ord. of 4-15-2025)
261:
(a) A law enforcement officer or animal services officer shall immediately impound a dog if the officer believes the dog poses a threat to the public safety.
(b) A classified dog shall be immediately impounded by any animal services officer or by a law enforcement officer in the case of any violation of this article. A refusal to surrender a dog subject to impoundment shall be a violation of this article.
(c) The owner of any dog that has been impounded pursuant to this article may recover such dog upon payment of all reasonable impoundment and housing costs and proof of compliance with the provisions of this article, unless such impoundment is deemed to be in error by an animal services officer or the county animal control board. All fines and all charges for services performed by a law enforcement or animal services officer shall be paid prior to owner recovery of the dog. Criminal prosecution shall not be stayed due to owner recovery or euthanasia of the dog.
(d) In the event the owner has not complied with the provisions of this article within 14 days of the date the dog was impounded, such dog shall be released to an animal shelter or euthanized in an expeditious and humane manner. The owner may be required to pay the costs of housing and euthanasia.
(Ord. of 4-15-2025)
262:
Upon a complaint lodged with the animal services division regarding any section of this article, a summons may be issued requiring the owner of any domesticated animal, or any person, firm or corporation violating any of the provisions set forth in this article to appear before the judge of the Cumming Municipal Court on a day and time certain to answer for the violation of this article. If such violation of this article has not been witnessed by an officer of the city, a subpoena may be issued to the person making the complaint, requiring such person to appear on the day and time of the hearing set by the court to testify on behalf of the city.
(Ord. of 4-15-2025)
263:

274:
The mayor and council do not wish to restrict dog ownership in the city and recognize that there are many properties and homes in the city that have adequate space, an appropriate environment for dogs, and are in compliance with the animal control ordinance. However, the mayor and council find that residents who violate the animal control ordinance affect the health, safety and welfare of other citizens who own, reside, or work in nearby properties. Citizens are affected by noise, dogs running at large, and are exposed to contamination and disease by poorly maintained properties that keep dogs in unclean or inadequate conditions. Therefore, the mayor and council find that it is in the best interest of the city to utilize its authority granted to the city to provide resources for animal services to review, track, and inspect properties following certain adjudicated violations of the animal control ordinance.
(Ord. of 4-15-2025)
275:
(a) A dog permit is required for any dog owner that is convicted three or more times within a two-year period for violating the animal code requirements regarding running at large, tethering, disturbing the peace, failure to vaccinate against rabies, or failure to quarantine.
(b) A dog permit is required for any dog owner if that owner is convicted for violating the animal code requirements regarding cruelty to animals, neglect of animals, or failure to follow requirements for keeping a classified dog. Additionally, a dog permit is required for any dog owner found guilty of a misdemeanor or felony violation of a state statute related to the care or treatment of animals within the past five years.
(c) This article shall apply to all properties in the city.
(d) For purposes of this section, conviction shall include an adjudication of guilty or plea of guilty or a plea of nolo contender.
(e) For purposes of this section, owner shall include anyone residing at a property where the dog(s) at issue for the conviction are kept and the number of citations under subsection (a) shall be totaled for such owners residing on the same property.
(f) In addition to complying with all applicable provisions of this chapter, any person obtaining a dog permit shall not allow the dogs to roam their property unleashed without a structural fence that provides an enclosed area from which the dogs cannot exit without human assistance.
(Ord. of 4-15-2025)

(a) Anyone requiring a dog permit shall complete an application with animal services within 15 days of a conviction that triggers the necessity of a permit.
(b) The application shall be accompanied by any payment method deemed acceptable by the city for the full amount of the permit fee in an amount to be set by the mayor and council.
(c) Each applicant shall certify that he or she has read and understands this chapter and the requirements for adequate food, shelter, space for dogs as well as the general requirements for owning or possessing dogs in the city.
(d) All applicants for a dog permit must consent to a reasonable inspection of the property and home where the dogs are kept. Such inspection may be performed before issuance of the permit or upon receipt of a complaint.
(e) If the person submitting an application is not the owner of the property at which the dogs will be kept, the applicant must submit an acknowledgement from the property owner that the applicant has permission to shelter or harbor the dogs on the property.
(Ord. of 4-15-2025)
277:
(a) Upon receipt of a complete application and payment of the application fee, the animal services director, or designee, will review to determine whether the applicant satisfies all the requirements as set out in this chapter. That review will include whether there is sufficient means to keep the dog(s) from running at large, whether rabies vaccinations are current, whether there are adequate facilities and means to insure that the dog(s) are kept in clean and humane conditions, free of contamination or disease, and in such a manner to minimize noise and odor.
(b) The animal services director, or designee thereof, may require any additional information and records he or she reasonably deems as necessary.
(c) The animal services director, or designee thereof, may require an inspection of the property as part of the evaluation and review of the application.

The animal services director shall schedule the appeal before the mayor and council and provide written notice of the time, place and date of that appeal. (a) [Establishment of rates, fees, service charges and deposits.] The rates, fees, service charges and deposits for water, sewer and stormwater as required under chapter 111, utilities, shall be as established by resolution of the mayor and city council. The Cumming Utilities Rate and Fee Schedule will be published online and on file in Cumming Department of Utilities. The rate and fee schedule will also be reviewed regularly and subject to adjustment by resolution of the mayor and city council and shall remain in effect until modified or amended by subsequent resolution or ordinance.
(b) Billing and administration of services.
(1) Establishing service. A deposit shall be required which is refundable after service termination and the final bill is paid in full. All new customers must submit picture identification, documentation of date of birth, a readable copy of a Georgia driver's license, a completed application for service along with either proof of ownership of the property such as a deed or a lease or rental agreement.
a. If the customer files for bankruptcy and the city is named in the bankruptcy, a new deposit will be required to re-establish service. The City of Cumming reserves the right to collect any past due debt.
b. The Director of Cumming Utilities Water, Sewer and Stormwater is authorized to require up to three times the applicable security deposit amount (above) for any consumer that the city has previously disconnected from service due to nonpayment. In addition, the Director of Cumming Utilities may require a consumer to pay outstanding water and sewer fees and charges owed by that consumer (including written-off debt and penalties assessed on past-due accounts) as a condition of establishing service.
c. It shall be the responsibility of the property owner or authorized agent(s) for the property receiving utility services from the city, to maintain current and proper contact and billing information on file with the city.
(2) Senior citizens (62 years and older) with picture ID. Senior citizens may receive a reduced billing on water services only (not on sewer service) for their primary residence. The reduced billing is calculated by applying a reduced percentage to the current monetary rates published for residential water users per gallons used.
(3) Garbage/solid waste collection within city limits. All property owners or their authorized agent(s) shall be required to pay for garbage/solid waste collection and disposal for all habitable property within the city and for the payment of fees to the city for such services. Garbage and solid waste collection fees are established by residential or commercial customer class and available to customers only within the City Limits of Cumming.
(4) Termination of services. Water, sewer and/or garbage services will be terminated for accounts not paid by the due date when balances are greater than $50.00 and any accounts more than 60 days past due.
(5) Penalties. When a meter is pulled or physically removed from active service for an account in bad standing due to non-payment, illegal action, code violation or similar conduct, a reconnection fee will be assessed to reestablish service. Customers or any unauthorized person(s) reconnecting without Cumming Utilities permission, and any damage to locks or meter parts caused by an unauthorized attempt to restore service will be subject to water meter tampering and damage fees.
a. When service is disconnected due to a delinquent backflow test, service will be restored only after all past due charges are paid in full including any service charges.
b. Nonpayment by the due date will incur a late payment fee penalty equal to ten percent of the customer's delinquent amount.
c. Returned check(s) or other rejected method of payment on an account will result in a charge as well as possible disconnection of service for nonpayment.
d. Payment methods utilizing credit cards will incur a processing fee as published in the rate and fee schedule.
(6) Delinquent accounts and collections. The Director of Cumming Utilities, or his/her authorized representative, shall have the authority to refer delinquent accounts including, but not limited to, fees, penalties and interest, to an agency for collection. The Director of Cumming Utilities, or his/her authorized representative, shall have the authority to write off accounts that are over one year old in an amount not to exceed $1,000.00 per account. "Write-off of debt" shall mean the accounting procedure by which the amount due is removed from the asset portion of the city's balance sheet.
a. The Director of Cumming Utilities may write off any such accounts in amounts between $1,000.01 and $50,000.00. The mayor and city council may write off any such accounts in amounts over $50,000.00. The write-off option shall be utilized only after it has been determined by the Director of Cumming Utilities that there is no cost-effective means for collecting the account. Writing off of debt is not legal forgiveness of debt.
b. Payment arrangements, or fee waivers may be authorized under exceptional circumstances only and as determined by the director of utilities. The city reserves the right to waive one month's penalty upon the consumer signing up for "Automated Draft Payments" (AutoPay) via Cumming Utilities online payment portal. Through the AutoPay agreement, the city will automatically debit the consumer's bank account or charge the consumer's credit card for the utility balance on the due date of the current bill. The consumer will receive this option once per account and will be expected to remain on AutoPay for at least one year.
(c) Water system charges.
(1) All metered customers will pay a base billing fee for water, sewer and garbage for each residential or commercial or industrial unit. For residential multi-unit developments, a water capacity charge will be assessed equivalent to the number of residential units multiplied by a set cost per unit as adopted by resolution in the Cumming Utilities Rate and Fee Schedule.
(2) Senior citizens reaching 62 years of age or older may apply for and receive reduced rates for water services only (sewer and garbage fees are not included in reduction). The reduced billing is charged as a percentage reduction from the published and adopted current residential water rates.
(3) Fire line and fire meter fees may be charged for customers with dedicated fire vault and fire lines. Monthly fire line use charges shall be established by a monthly base fee according to the fire meter size to recover city costs of testing, maintenance, and other non-documented fire responses. In addition to the base fee, fire line water rates shall be uniform and applied by usage per 1,000 gallons as published and adopted by resolution in the rate and fee schedule. All fire vaults and piping shall comply with article IV, cross connection and backflow, section 111-110, requirements.
(4) Water system fees (capacity and connection) are calculated based on the following and published in the city's rate and fee schedule:
a. Water capacity fees for all customer classes except multi-unit properties, shall be charged based on meter size and as published in the rate and fee schedule adopted by resolution. For multi-unit properties, the capacity fee shall be calculated by applying an established unit cost per the number of units.
(5) Special water service fees have been established by the mayor and city council and as published in the rate and fee schedule. These fees include the following;
a. Customer requested testing (calibration) of the water meter, or relocation of the meter shall incur a one-time charge per meter. The charge for a customer requested relocation for meters larger than one inch will also include materials cost.
b. Customer requested reading of the meter other than the regularly scheduled meter read will incur a fee.
(6) Fire hydrant meter rental fees shall require a deposit, of which a portion shall be refunded once the meter is returned in good condition. Additionally, water usage will be charged based on current published commercial irrigation water rates.
(7) Stolen, damaged, or misplaced meters will incur a fine and fees including illegal removal of a lock, and meter tampering. The meter includes register, antenna, backflow, meter box, lid, curb-stop and any appurtenances of the city's water system.
(8) Temporary water service connection to the city's water system for approved purposes shall only be made by fire hydrant using a city obtained hydrant meter and permit. A security deposit will be required upon receipt of the permit and will be applied to the final bill. A usage fee will be applied according to the utilities rate and fee schedule and a late fee charged per day for hydrant meters not returned on the assigned day to be read. The meter permit allows use of the meter according to all specifications and requirements for fire hydrant usage as directed by the city.
(d) Sewer system charges. There is hereby charged and assessed to each property, premises or facility served by the water pollution control facilities (WPCF) or publicly owned treatment works (POTW) of the city, or otherwise discharging wastewater, industrial wastes, water or liquids, either directly or indirectly into the WPCF, a sewer service base fee and service rate assessment payable as hereinafter provided, and in the amounts determinable as follows:
(1) The sewer service charge shall be based upon the quantity of water used by the premises or facility therein or thereon as measured by a water meter or meters there in use, or as otherwise currently established.
(2) The sewer service rate shall consist of a base fee and charge per 1,000 gallons of water consumed, including any adjustments. Rates shall be established for each customer class.
(3) Any industrial or commercial customer that discharges wastewater produced on site, including without limitation, landfill leachate, shall meter all wastewater at the point of discharge to the sewer collection system, and the sewer service charge will be calculated from that metered flow.
(4) Additional sewer system surcharge fees may be levied against customers whose effluent concentration(s) exceed the maximum allowable wastewater concentrations established under section 111-134. (a) It is the intent and purpose of this division to regulate the place of operation of adult entertainment establishments. This division is intended to be a carefully tailored regulation to minimize the adverse land use impacts caused by the undesirable secondary effects of adult entertainment establishments. The mayor and council find that restricting adult entertainment establishments to industrially zoned areas and imposing development standards can legitimately regulate adult entertainment establishments by establishing zones where adult entertainment establishments are most compatible with other uses or the surrounding neighborhood, and by requiring minimum distances to be maintained between adult entertainment establishment uses and other uses so as to afford the most protection to residential uses. It is not the intent or purpose of the mayor and council, in enacting this division, to deny to any person rights to speech, conduct or expression protected by the United States or state constitution. In the enactment of this division, the mayor and council intend to adopt a content-neutral measure to address the secondary effects of adult entertainment establishments.
(b) Based on the experiences of other communities and municipalities, on studies, reports and findings of other communities, specifically, Indianapolis, Indiana; Austin, Texas; State of Minnesota; St. Paul, Minnesota; and Roswell, Georgia, which are experiences and findings relevant to the problems that concern the city insofar as the growth of adult entertainment establishments, and after hearing expert testimony, it is noted that many types of criminal activity are frequently engendered by such businesses; and such businesses tend to create undesirable community conditions under certain circumstances, particularly circumstances related to the sale and consumption of alcoholic beverages. Among the acts identified with such establishments are disorderly conduct, prostitution, drug trafficking and drug use. Among the undesirable community conditions identified with such establishments are depression in property values in the surrounding neighborhood, increased expenditure for and allocation of law enforcement personnel to preserve law and order, increased burden on the judicial system as a consequence of criminal behavior and acceleration of community blight by the concentration of such establishments in particular areas. Specifically, the problems associated with increased prostitution, DUIs and other vice problems peak at the same times as other crimes that would require more resources for law enforcement. The types of operations that are used to curb prostitution and DUIs are labor-intensive and time-consuming with significant costs. The nearby neighborhoods suffer from increased noise levels during early morning hours and increased vandalism, including urination in doorways. Accordingly, the purpose of this division is to regulate certain types of business, including but not limited to adult entertainment establishments, to the end that the many types of criminal activities frequently engendered by such businesses will be curtailed. However, it is recognized that such regulation cannot de facto approach prohibition. Otherwise, a protected form of expression would vanish. As to adult entertainment establishments, this division represents a balancing of competing interests; reduced criminal activity and protection of the neighborhoods through the regulation of adult entertainment establishments versus the protected rights of adult entertainment establishments and patrons thereof.
(c) The mayor and council find, based on a 1984 study entitled Adult Entertainment Businesses in Indianapolis, that areas with sexually oriented businesses had higher crime rates than similar areas with no sexually oriented business. Specifically, the mayor and council find that the study reveals that sex-related crimes, defined in the study as rape, indecent exposure, obscene conduct, child molestation, adult molestation, and commercial sex, are much more prevalent in areas where adult entertainment is offered than in areas where no adult entertainment is offered. The same finding is true as to the occurrence of major crimes.
(d) The mayor and council further find, based on a May 19, 1986, study from Austin, Texas, entitled Report on Adult Oriented Businesses in Austin, that severe decline in residential property values may be precipitated by the presence of an adult entertainment establishment, particularly where that adult entertainment establishment is located within one block of residential property uses. Furthermore, the mayor and council find that there is an indication that the introduction of adult entertainment establishments into areas of family-oriented, owner-occupied residential neighborhoods may precipitate a transition to a more transient, renter-occupied neighborhood.
(e) The mayor and council further find, based on an October 1980 study by the Minnesota Crime Prevention Center, Inc., Minneapolis, Minnesota, entitled An Analysis of the Relationship Between Adult Entertainment Establishments, Crime and Housing Values, that adult businesses do have a significant and consistent positive correlation with the crime rate index and a negative correlation with the mean single-family housing value. The mayor and council also find, based on this study, that adult entertainment businesses should be permitted only in locations that are at least one-tenth mile, or approximately 500 feet, from residential areas and that adult entertainment businesses should not be placed adjacent to one another.
(f) The mayor and council further find, based on a June 1978 study from St. Paul, Minnesota, entitled Effects on Surrounding Area of Adult Entertainment Businesses in Saint Paul, that the presence of adult entertainment establishments correlates statistically with poor neighborhood condition. The mayor and council further find, based on this study, that the location of adult entertainment establishments correlates significantly with neighborhood deterioration.
(g) Moreover, it is the finding of the mayor and council that public nudity, either partial or total, under certain circumstances, particularly circumstances related to the sale and/or consumption of alcoholic beverages in adult entertainment establishments leads to an increase in the surrounding area of criminal behavior and creates undesirable community conditions, blight and diminution in property values.

(a) No adult entertainment establishment shall be located:
(1) Within 500 feet of any parcel of land zoned or used for residential uses or purposes.
(2) Within 500 feet of any parcel of land upon which a church, school, government building, day care facility, library, civic center, public park, or playground is located.
(3) Within 500 feet of any parcel of land upon which another establishment regulated or defined under this division is located.
(4) Within 100 yards of any parcel of land upon which any other establishment selling alcoholic beverages is located.
(5) On less than one acre of land containing at least 150 feet of road frontage.
(6) In any district other than one that is zoned for and meets all requirements of M-1 zoning district.
(b) For the purposes of this section, distance shall be from property line to property line along the shortest possible straight-line distance, regardless of any customary or common route or path of travel, i.e., as the crow flies. The term "parcel of land" means any quantity of land capable of being described by location and boundary.
(Code 1998, § 10-57; Ord. of 2-18-1997, § I-7)
